prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one objectively “best” broker for every self‑employed person — the right broker depends on your priorities (price, local in‑person help, experience with ACA subsidies, familiarity with specialty plans, ongoing service). Below are practical recommendations and steps to help you pick the best health insurance broker in Kansas City, MO for your situation.

Who to consider
- Local independent brokers/agents in Kansas City who focus on ACA individual & family plans and small‑business/sole‑proprietor needs. They can help with provider networks, local claims issues, and ongoing service.
- National online brokers/marketplaces (e.g., eHealth, HealthSherpa, HealthMarkets, GoHealth). Good for getting quick plan comparisons across carriers and help with Marketplace enrollment/subsidies.
- Navigators and community enrollment assisters (free) — they can help you enroll in Marketplace plans and determine subsidy eligibility but may not sell commercial plans.
- Accountants or benefits consultants who work with self‑employed clients (if you want tax-aware plan design such as HSAs).

What to look for in a broker
- Active Missouri insurance license (verify on Missouri Department of Insurance producer lookup).
- Experience with the ACA individual market, premium tax credits (subsidies), and advance premium tax credit reconciliation.
- Familiarity with HSAs, QSEHRA/SEHRA (if you offer a benefit to yourself/employees), and short‑term vs ACA distinctions.
- Transparent compensation model (commission vs flat fee) and whether they’ll work on renewals / claims help.
- Good online reviews and references from other self‑employed clients.

Questions to ask any broker
- Do you help enroll in Marketplace plans and check subsidy eligibility?
- How are you compensated? Will I pay you a fee?
- How many self‑employed clients do you serve?
- Do you assist with claims or renewals if problems arise?
- Can you provide references from Kansas City clients?
- Are you licensed in Missouri? (ask for license number)

Practical steps
1. Decide if you need an ACA-compliant plan (individual market) vs short‑term or association plans (short‑term generally not ACA-compliant and may offer limited coverage).
2. Check subsidy eligibility on healthCare.gov (or have the broker run estimates).
3. Get quotes from 2–3 brokers — one local independent agent, one national marketplace, and one navigator/assister — and compare premiums, networks, deductibles, and out‑of‑pocket maxes.
4. Verify the broker’s Missouri license and read recent reviews/BBB listing.
5. Enroll during Open Enrollment (or see if you qualify for a Special Enrollment Period).

If you want, I can:
- Look up highly rated local Kansas City brokers/agents (I’ll need your ZIP code or neighborhood), or
- Run through a short checklist tailored to your budget, preferred doctors, and health needs to help you narrow options.
